$comment: CROSS-LANGUAGE CONTRACT FIXTURE — one shared definition of where a Vega-Lite spec's rows live, and which specs are in contract at all. Consumed by web/app/lib/__tests__/chart-row-extraction.contract.test.ts (specDataRows / specViolatesContract / MAX_SPEC_DEPTH) and by the pytest for ChartSpec on the backend. Both implementations must agree on every case here. This file exists because the two sides drifted: the client walked nested containers while the server read the root only, and NEITHER resolved altair's default named-dataset shape — so one spec produced three different answers (client-envelope: empty, client-bare: drawn, server: 'No data.'). Add a case here BEFORE fixing a row-extraction or validation bug on either side, so the fix has to land on both.
$definition: ROWS: (1) the root's `data`, (2) any nested container's `data` — layer / concat / hconcat / vconcat / spec, (3) a named reference `data: {name}` resolved against the ROOT `datasets` map. Inline `values` wins over a named reference on the same node ONLY WHEN NON-EMPTY: vega-lite@6.4.3 resolves `{name: 'd', values: []}` to the named dataset, verified by compiling it. The first container that yields rows wins; containers are searched in the order listed. A row is a JSON object; non-object array elements (numbers, strings) are legal payload but are not rows and do not count. WALK DEPTH: both implementations cap at `limits.maxDepth`, counting every JSON level; a spec deeper than the cap is refused rather than silently half-read. IN CONTRACT: an inline payload under `values` or `datasets` must be an ARRAY — nothing more. Vega-Lite's InlineDataset legitimately admits string[] / number[] / boolean[] (a sort order, a tick set), and refusing those rejected specs vl_convert renders fine. The array test is the whole safety argument: the walk deliberately skips the CONTENTS of `values`/`datasets` so a data column named `url` is not a false positive, and what that skip must not let through is a DICT — spec structure smuggled past the walk. `[1,2,3]` contains no dict and smuggles nothing. A CSV/TSV STRING under `values` is OUT of contract and rejected by both sides even though vega parses it: the design promises the data ships alongside every chart so a reader can expand it to a table, and a CSV string neither side parses cannot be tabulated — accepting it would render a picture whose numbers are unreadable, silently breaking the provenance promise that is the whole trust story.

limits.$note: Ruled 64 on both sides. Previously unpinned drift: the client capped at 64 and the server at 16, agreeing up to 16 and diverging from 17. Written here so it is a contract value, not two constants that happen to match.
